objective: Test on this lab's own archived run histories whether the residual level at which a run is declared converged actually bounds how much the graded quantity still moves afterwards, and compare that remaining drift against the tolerance the run was graded on
rationale: Nearly every credential this lab holds rests on a convergence declaration made against a residual threshold, and a residual is a property of the equations rather than of the number that gets graded. The lab already owns the counterexample in another form: a rotor case diverged behind converged residuals, and the standing replay item exists precisely because monitored quantities went somewhere the residuals did not report. That is one case. The question here is what the proportion is across everything already on disk, and the archive is large enough to answer it without a single new solve: 595 log files sit under the archived run tree on this host, spanning the adjoint, closure, verification and rotor families. THE NULL, AND IT IS NOT FITTED: both numbers pre-exist the analysis and neither is chosen by it. The residual threshold was written into each run's configuration before that run started; the grading tolerance was written into each pre-registration before its verdict. This item selects nothing and tunes nothing; it reads two frozen numbers and one trajectory. THE IDENTITY TEST, owner rule W dash 2, and it is the reason the gate is shaped the way it is rather than the obvious way. The obvious formulation would be to correlate residual level against remaining drift. THAT WOULD BE NEARLY AN IDENTITY AND IT IS REFUSED HERE: both quantities are computed from the same iteration history and both decay toward the end of a converging run, so a strong positive correlation is guaranteed by construction and would carry no information about anything. This lab has already paid for that lesson once, with a correlation of 0.9742 that was uninformative because its null sat pinned at unity. The gated quantity here is instead an ABSOLUTE comparison against an externally set number: is the remaining drift larger than the tolerance that run was graded against? The tolerance comes from a pre-registration written by a different person at a different time for a different purpose, and no construction connects it to the iteration history, so the comparison is not an identity.
gate: ZERO SOLVER COMPUTE; arithmetic over histories already on disk. Per archived run with a recoverable history and a recoverable grading tolerance: find the iteration at which the residual criterion was first met, and measure how far the graded quantity moved between that iteration and the run's end, as a fraction of the grading tolerance. Three-valued per run. BOUNDED if the remaining movement is inside the tolerance. UNBOUNDED if it exceeds it, which means the residual criterion did not bound the graded answer for that run. NO VERDICT if either the threshold or the tolerance cannot be recovered from the record, counted and reported rather than dropped, because a silently dropped run is how the denominator gets flattering. HEADLINE: the three counts with the frame stated, plus the fraction unbounded. WHAT WOULD CHANGE PRACTICE: if the unbounded fraction is material, then a plateau-in-the-graded-quantity criterion has to sit beside the residual criterion in every gate, and the affected credentials need re-derivation or a caveat. WHAT THE ITEM MAY NOT DO: it may not re-grade any credential and it may not touch any pre-registration. It reports, and files residuals to the docket under fresh append-only identifiers. CONTROL, mandatory and reported first: at least one run known to have settled cleanly must classify as bounded, and at least one run from the rotor family known to have gone somewhere behind converged residuals must classify as unbounded. A classifier that cannot recover the known case in each direction does not get to report a fraction.
cost_basis: ZERO solver compute. Scored in agent tool calls: forecast 55, in the upper half of this lab's measured build-and-verify band of 33 to 72, because the item writes a parser against several log formats, runs it over a large archive and hand-recovers grading tolerances from pre-registrations. Actual counted from the executing agent's transcript. Anchored on one measured fact rather than a guess about size: the archive was enumerated during the drafting of this proposal at 1 tool call and holds 595 log files under the archived run tree on this host, and the parser rather than the volume is the cost. The recovery rate of grading tolerances is the largest unknown and is stated as such; if it is poor the no-verdict count will dominate, which is itself the finding.
expected_knowledge_gain: THE DISCRIMINATING OUTCOME. If a material fraction of archived runs is unbounded, then residual-threshold convergence is not a sufficient gate in this lab and every credential resting on one needs a graded-quantity plateau criterion beside it; that is a change to how every future gate is written, bought from data already paid for. If the fraction is near zero with both controls recovered, the practice is vindicated on evidence rather than on habit, and the rotor case is correctly understood as the exception it is currently treated as. The outcome that would move nothing is a no-verdict count that swamps the other two, and the gate reports that as a records defect rather than as a result about convergence.
hard_criterion_note: Starts no flow case. Arithmetic over completed runs whose histories are already on disk.

launch_prompt: Residual threshold against graded drift, retrospective. ZERO COMPUTE, and launch no solver under any circumstances. Step 1: establish and REPORT both controls before any fraction is computed, as the gate requires. Step 2: write the parser and state which log formats it handles and which it does not; a format it cannot read is a no-verdict, not a skip. Step 3: classify, and state the frame of every count. Step 4: report the three counts and the fraction unbounded. Do NOT re-grade any credential and do NOT edit any pre-registration; file residuals to the docket with fresh append-only identifiers.
